name: Gambia

findings.financier: Export-Import Bank of China (concessional loan, on-lent via Government of the Gambia)
findings.summary: The Gambia National Broadband Network, at least 420 km of fibre plus a data centre extending the ECOWAN/WARCIP backbone, was implemented by Huawei and Gamtel on a China Exim loan and commissioned in June 2019.

sources.publisher: World Broadband Association / Gamtel case study

findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: Huawei named as implementer by AidData; WBBA confirms the 420 km NBN, Gamtel ownership and US$25m China Exim loan but names no vendor, and is an S4 industry document, so not counted for corroboration. Value is the loan-agreement figure reported by AidData. Gamtel data centre in the package not coded separately (vendor and status unknown).

findings.summary: Gamtel signed a partnership with Huawei to modernise and extend its core network backbone, with Huawei deploying seven DWDM units and OLTs to raise capacity; no value or financing was disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3 is a reviewer call: a signed agreement with named equipment scope but no value; could be tier 2 if it is a framework only. Deployment status not confirmed.

findings.summary: QCell, the second-largest mobile operator (about 28% share), launched The Gambia's first commercial 5G service in selected Banjul-area locations, with Huawei as its technology partner.
findings.analyst_inference: Sources call Huawei QCell's technology partner/technical support rather than explicitly the RAN supplier; inferred vendor. Tier 4 not 5 because coverage was limited to a few Banjul-area sites at launch. QCell's parent QGroup describes Huawei as a 17-year partner (The Point, 2026).

findings.local_actor: All four mobile operators (Africell, QCell, Gamcel, Comium)
findings.summary: The US Commerce Department's country commercial guide states Huawei has installed the network cabling for all four Gambian network providers, naming no other vendor.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S1 source; the statement is broad and does not distinguish radio, core or transmission equipment. Operator list taken from Ecofin's citation of regulator PURA market shares. Overlaps GMB-001 to GMB-003; read as evidence of Huawei incumbency across operators.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy
findings.summary: At Gitex Africa 2024 the ministry signed an MoU naming UAE firm Presight its digital-transformation partner: phase one digital government services, national digital ID and a national data centre; phase two a national safety operations centre.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: Presight is majority-owned by G42 (UAE). MoU only; no value, contract or delivery found. The national data centre component, if built, would be a separate facilities finding; owner-operator unknown.

findings.summary: President Barrow inaugurated QGroup House in April 2026, an eight-storey building housing what was presented as The Gambia's first data centre; no capacity, tier rating, vendor or cost was given.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic: QGroup is a Gambian conglomerate (parent of QCell); the article does not state the operating entity. Inauguration date inferred as Wednesday 29 April 2026. Tier 4 because operation at scale is not described. Huawei is QCell's long-time partner but is not named as data-centre supplier.

research_gaps: Second submarine cable (World Bank WARDIP, ~US$30-35m, Gambia–Guinea MoU April 2024): has a supplier been selected and on what terms (BOT)? Not coded because no vendor is named.
Africell (about 63% share) radio/core vendor not established; trade.gov claim of Huawei across all four operators needs operator-level confirmation.
Did the Presight MoU lead to a contract for the national data centre, digital ID or safety operations centre?
Is the Gamtel data centre built under the China Exim NBN project still operating, and who supplied its IT equipment?
Was the Gamtel–Huawei backbone upgrade (Oct 2023) delivered, and is YCELL's acquisition of 80% of Gamcel (July 2026) changing vendors? YCELL's nationality unknown.
No safe-city/CCTV deal found in one search; check airport security-equipment donation reports and any police surveillance procurement.
